=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~5006-~5017 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN` is expanded inside a double-quoted `grep` invocation, so shell expansion or command substitution can alter the regex before `grep` evaluates it.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on impact, ranging from low-risk matching drift to worst-case command-substitution risk, but all cited the same unquoted-pattern bug.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~5009-~5031 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The warning messages log `^orchestrator/project-[0-9]+$`, but the fallback Bash regex actually used for `BASH_REMATCH` is `^orchestrator/project-([0-9]+)$`.
  WHY: The mismatch is diagnostic only, but it can mislead operators who copy the warning text when debugging pattern failures.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~5018-~5026 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: When `grep` rejects the configured pattern, the warning path leaves `_orch_is_integration_pr` false and still falls through to the canonical regex test, so the fallback behavior described in the warning is not what the code actually does.
  WHY: An invalid custom pattern can produce a warning that suggests a fallback while the eventual suppression decision still depends on the later canonical match, creating confusing diagnostics.
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:596-602 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new contract test only checks for literal YAML text and does not exercise runtime behavior of the configurable orchestrator branch pattern.
  WHY: A regression in the grep/fallback logic or pattern-supplied behavior would not be caught by this test.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~4990-~5000 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The fallback stderr file path is built from `RUNNER_TEMP`/`GITHUB_WORKSPACE`/`PWD` without guaranteeing a unique writable location.
  WHY: Concurrent jobs or unwritable workspaces could lose error details and degrade diagnostics, even though the flow fails closed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml + README.md:ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN usage + doc updates | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Older pinned workflow wrappers or cached YAML may miss the new env line that makes the auto-merge suppressor consume `ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN`.
  WHY: In those deployments, suppression would fall back only to the canonical regex and the contract test does not cover the full integration path.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~5006 grep -Eq -- "${ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN}" | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The ORCH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH_PATTERN value is interpolated inside double quotes in a bash pipeline, so any dollar sign or backtick character in the pattern value would undergo shell expansion before grep receives it.
  WHY: Would only trigger if an admin intentionally sets the repo variable to a pattern containing a literal `$` anchor or backticks — extremely unlikely for a branch-name regex.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:~5009, ~5014 warning messages | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The two warning messages log the fallback regex as `^orchestrator/project-[0-9]+$` (no capturing parentheses), but the actual canonical fallback code on the next lines uses `^orchestrator/project-([0-9]+)$` (with capturing parentheses for `BASH_REMATCH`).
  WHY: This is cosmetic only — it does not affect runtime behavior, since the `BASH_REMATCH` code path uses the correct capturing regex.
